messages:
From: Brenda Cole <brenda.cole@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Modular VPC deployment - reference brief & acceptance criteria

Marcus,

Thanks for taking the time to review our on-prem requirements. We want a compact reference brief that captures the control-plane / data-plane split for our tenant topology and a clear list of acceptance criteria for network handoff to our SREs. High level:

- Control plane runs in customer-managed VPC with a small set of control endpoints (management API, auth, telemetry egress).
- Data plane (inference nodes) will live on isolated subnets with strict egress controls.
- We need clear egress proofing guidance and a short checklist so our ops team can validate the cutover.

Attached: a short inventory of our rack-level IP plan (acme-infra-inventory.csv). Can you provide a short reference diagram and an acceptance checklist we can use for sign-off?

We'd like to lock the acceptance criteria by EOD so the integration window next week is smooth.

Thanks,
Brenda Cole
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

NOTE: Attachment stub: acme-infra-inventory.csv (CSV, 24 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Brenda Cole <brenda.cole@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Modular VPC deployment - reference brief & acceptance criteria

Brenda — thanks, good summary. I attached a short reference diagram and a first-pass acceptance checklist that map to your inventory. Highlights / design assumptions:

- Control plane endpoints: we expect a small NATed control-plane subnet for outbound telemetry -> allow TLS to telemetry endpoints only; management API endpoints accept mTLS from pinned service accounts.
- Data plane isolation: inference pools per-tenant in separate subnets + strict security groups; KV cache traffic is internal to the rack fabric.
- Egress proofing: we provide test scripts (curl checks, DNS egress test, port-scan) and a sequence of validation steps for your SREs.

Acceptance checklist (short):
1) Control plane reachability (mTLS validated using provisioned client cert)
2) Data plane subnet routing (no default route to public internet)
3) Egress rules verified against telemetry host FQNs and ports
4) Failover verified (control-plane endpoint fallback to secondary region)
5) KV cache encryption at rest verified

Attachments: modular-vpc-ref-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram, 1.1 MB), modular-deploy-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18 KB)

Can Kimberly and Irene quickly sanity-check the checklist items below (especially the failover test and KMS notes) and then Brenda if that looks good we can formalize the sign-off steps.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: modular-vpc-ref-diagram-v1.pdf; modular-deploy-acceptance-checklist.xlsx

Quick notes after a pass:

- Failover: clarify the expected RTO for control-plane failover. Proposal: 90s for DNS TTL-based failover + health-check propagation. Call this out in the checklist under step 4.
- KMS: add a verification bullet that customer KMS alias is accessible from the control-plane subnet (we cannot assume KMS peering).
- Egress proofing: add a deterministic order to tests: (1) DNS resolution for telemetry FQNs, (2) TLS handshake to telemetry host, (3) confirm no HTTP fallback.

I updated the checklist spreadsheet with these items (minor). Marcus — please add the RTO note to the diagram caption and confirm whether the control-plane will publish a health endpoint we can poll during testing.

Kimberly Park
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Kimberly / Irene — this is great, thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple quick confirmations from our side after reviewing the checklist:

- We accept the proposed RTO of 90s for control-plane failover. We'll surface any SLA exceptions if our change window requires tighter bounds.
- KMS verification: our key team confirmed the alias will be reachable from the control-plane subnet; we'll add a short runbook step to verify access and rotate a test secret.
- Egress proofing order is good. Ops will run tests in the sequence Kimberly suggested and attach results to the confluence page.

Next steps per timeline:
- Today: Redwood updates diagram caption with RTO note and pushes final checklist (Marcus).
- Tomorrow AM: Acme runs the inventory-derived validation and shares PASS/FAIL per checklist item (Brenda).
- After PASS: we schedule the integration cutover for next Tuesday (change window already booked).
